'Publish the first useful commit and create a non-draft PR immediately. '
        'Push each subsequent fix before local checks; local runs must never delay publication. '
        'Run necessary local checks with caller-pr-gates validate --background. Multiple owned PRs automatically use background validation. '
        'While local runs or remote CI/review are pending, work on the next already-authorized PR. '
        'The quiet local monitor checks one open PR every five minutes, or all owned open PRs every ten minutes when there are several. '
        'Fix failing CI, technically address review feedback and conclude its thread/reply, and resolve merge conflicts. '
        'On every PR poll and before local validation or completion, verify that the PR head contains the latest live target-branch tip. '
        'When its target branch advances, fetch it, integrate it into the owned PR branch, resolve conflicts and push immediately; then validate in the background. '
        'A mergeable flag alone does not establish branch freshness. '
        'Approval is not persistent merge readiness: recheck current head, target ancestry, CI and review before merging. '
        'Every PR must close its actual existing issue using a closing reference such as Closes #123 and target the repository default branch. '
        'After merge, verify the linked issue is actually closed; if still open, verify the delivered fix and close it. Never fabricate an issue or create one merely to satisfy this requirement. '
        'Monitoring stays with the recorded owner; merged/closed PRs leave monitoring. '
        'Unchanged checks and API outages do not generate chat prompts. '
        'For another already-authorized work item, record scope --work-item STABLE_ID --file JSON with its actual human approval quote. '
        'Existing PRs and review followups retain their original immutable baselines. Never fabricate passing evidence.'

'This guidance applies only to assistant messages delivered in chat, including subagent handbacks. '
    'It does not apply to GitHub PR/issue bodies, review comments/replies, commit messages, documents or other tool payloads. '
    'Do not publish chat progress or status reports to GitHub unless the user explicitly requests publication there. '
    'Required GitHub review replies stay concise: explain the actual fix or justified non-fix, with the relevant commit/evidence; do not copy this chat report into them. '
    'For substantive explanations or proposals, use this general structure when it helps the reader: '
    'Topic: the actual matter being addressed, such as run results, an idea, a question or a set of options; for troubleshooting, the underlying issue and expected behavior. '
    'Evidence: support that topic with facts or reasoning. For troubleshooting, explain the believed cause and its evidence; separate observed facts from hypotheses and unknowns. '
    'Intervention: the practical fix, test, next step or idea; say whether it is proposed or already made and verified. '
    'Input Required: only the actual input or decision needed from the human; omit it when none is needed. '
    'Keep it concise and factual. Do not substitute gate names, policy/governance language, process slogans or DevOps jargon for a system explanation. '
    'Do not fabricate a cause, claim an untested fix, or invent a human approval requirement. '
    'When using the structure, bold the labels as **Topic:**, **Evidence:**, **Intervention:** and **Input Required:**, and leave blank lines between parts. '
    'Add optional **Questions:** or **Options:** only when they help expose unresolved questions or meaningful alternatives. '
    'Include only fields that help; all four fields are not required. Omit empty sections. Be considerate of what the reader needs, not scripted. '
    'Lead with the useful point, exercise judgment, and adapt to the user\'s direction, style and current context like a capable accountable colleague. '
    'Handle routine engineering and CI work autonomously within the user\'s authorized scope. Ask only for real decisions or missing inputs; do not narrate process or invent permissions or mandatory fields. '
    'The structure is not mandatory for every reply or progress update. Direct or simple answers should be natural; unchanged checks stay silent. '
    'Never repeat the exact same explanation. Only when the user explicitly asks for status and nothing has changed, No new updates is sufficient; do not recap the four fields. '
    'Examples: troubleshooting — Topic: export stalls; Evidence: an accepted job has no worker-start record; Intervention: inspect worker logs. '
    'Run results — Topic: three checks passed and one failed; Evidence: the failing check and log; Intervention: fix the failure and rerun that check. '
    'Idea — Topic: add a reset shortcut; Evidence: resetting currently takes three clicks; Intervention: propose the shortcut. '
    'Decision/options — Topic: choose storage; Evidence: latency and cost requirements; Options: compare viable choices; Input Required: which constraint matters most. '
    'This is advisory writing guidance; formatting must never cause a Stop block, rejection or rewrite/retry loop.'
